title: Meatloaf
subtitle: A classic American baked beef and pork loaf with a ketchup glaze
excerpt: Seasoned beef and pork mince with onion and breadcrumbs, baked in a loaf pan and glazed with ketchup for a sticky, caramelised top. Firm enough to slice, tender enough to eat with a fork.
sourceNotes: Classic American diner meatloaf, adapted from traditional mid-century American home cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked and cooled loaf whole or in slices. Reheat from frozen at 180C until piping hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the loaf a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Add 10 minutes to the bake time if going in cold.

content.text: Meatloaf is a straightforward baked loaf of seasoned mince, held together with egg and breadcrumbs and finished with a sticky ketchup glaze. The mix of beef and pork keeps it moist. Do not overmix once the wet ingredients go in, or the finished loaf will be dense and tight.
Heat the oven to 190C. Melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the diced onion with a pinch of salt for 8 minutes until soft and translucent. Tip onto a plate and leave to cool.
Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes until absorbed.
Put the beef mince, pork mince, cooled onion, soaked breadcrumbs, eggs, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Mix with your hands until just combined. Do not overwork.
Pack the mixture into a 900g loaf tin and level the top. Spread the ketchup evenly over the surface.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 70C and the glaze is dark and sticky.
Rest in the tin for 10 minutes before turning out. Slice with a sharp knife.

items.cause: Lean mince was used, or it overbaked.
items.fix: Use mince with at least 15 to 20% fat content, and take the loaf out as soon as it reaches 70C inside.

items.symptom: The loaf falls apart when sliced.
items.cause: Not enough binder, or the loaf was cut too soon.
items.fix: Allow the full 10-minute rest before slicing, and make sure the breadcrumb and egg quantities are correct.

items.cause: The oven runs hot or the tin was placed too high.
items.fix: Move the tin to the lower third of the oven and lay a piece of foil loosely over the top for the last 15 minutes if the glaze darkens too fast.
